toyota_summary:
China's largest battery maker CATL is accelerating production capacity in partnership with a local producer, signaling confidence that Chinese EV makers will capture more of the global market even as Western automakers struggle with profitability in that region. The expansion comes as China doubles down on battery technology as a strategic priority, embedding supply chain control into its industrial policy.

This matters because battery costs determine EV margins everywhere. If CATL expands faster than Western competitors can match, Chinese automakers gain a structural cost advantage that compounds over time. European and American manufacturers already face tighter emissions rules and slower EV adoption at home—losing the battery cost race would squeeze them from both ends.

Watch whether European automakers use this week's earnings calls to signal price cuts or production cuts in response to Chinese competition.

emails.summary_en: Toyota announced plans to invest in Thailand to produce a fuel-cell electric pickup truck, with operations slated to begin in December 2027. The move underscores automakers' continued bets on hydrogen-based powertrains for commercial vehicles even as battery EVs dominate near-term adoption. Thailand's growing role as a regional hub for next-generation vehicle manufacturing is reinforced by the investment.

emails.subject: Franco-German deal won’t rescue Europe’s auto industry
emails.subject_en: Franco-German deal won’t rescue Europe’s auto industry
emails.summary_en: France and Germany struck a deal easing EU emissions targets for automakers while tightening 'Made in Europe' content rules, helping unblock two stalled industry bills in Brussels. Critics argue the softened 2035 target—now 90% emissions cuts instead of full elimination—gives European carmakers less incentive to invest in EV technology just as Chinese rivals like Leapmotor surge ahead. Meanwhile, German automakers continue cutting jobs and closing plants, raising fears the compromise favors political expediency over competitiveness.
emails.summary_ja: フランスとドイツは、EUの自動車排出目標を緩和する一方で「欧州製」部品比率の規制を強化する合意に達し、ブリュッセルで停滞していた2つの産業政策法案の打開につながった。批評家は、2035年目標が完全排出ゼロから90%削減へと緩和されたことで、欧州メーカーのEV技術投資への意欲が弱まり、急成長する中国メーカー(Leapmotorなど)にさらに後れを取る恐れがあると指摘する。その間にもドイツの自動車メーカーは人員削減や工場閉鎖を続けており、今回の妥協が産業競争力よりも政治的便宜を優先したとの懸念が広がっている。
